content.user_title: Find Code Patterns with AST Search
content.value_statement: Regex misses structural code patterns during reviews and refactors. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use ast-grep for precise searches, rewrites, and rule scans.
actual_capabilities: Provides ast-grep command patterns for functions, imports, React hooks, async code, and language constructs.
Shows JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust search examples.
Guides preview and applied rewrites with ast-grep replacement syntax.
Documents reusable YAML rules, rule tests, and project configuration.
Includes security pattern searches for XSS, secrets, command injection, path traversal, and unsafe deserialization.
Shows integrations with jq, fd, fzf, pre-commit, CI, and VS Code.
limitations: Requires the ast-grep CLI to be installed and available as sg.
Search patterns may need language-specific tuning for complex syntax.
Applied rewrites can change files and should be reviewed before committing.
Security matches identify suspicious patterns but do not prove exploitability.

use_cases.title: Audit Code During Review
use_cases.description: Find repeated risky patterns, framework mistakes, or cleanup targets before merging changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Large Refactors
use_cases.description: Locate old APIs, preview replacements, and estimate the scope of a migration.

use_cases.title: Build Team Search Rules
use_cases.description: Create reusable ast-grep rules for project conventions, lint checks, and CI enforcement.

prompt_templates.title: Find Simple Usages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural-search to find every call to [function] in this repository. Show files, match context, and suggested follow-up checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Framework Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural-search to inspect [framework] patterns for [risk or convention]. Group matches by likely action needed.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural-search to preview replacing [old pattern] with [new pattern]. Report match categories and risks before applying changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create CI Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural-search to design ast-grep rules for [policy]. Include rule purpose, test coverage, and CI usage guidance.

output_examples.output: The skill returns matching files, groups logging by usage type, and recommends which entries are safe to remove.

output_examples.input: Plan a migration from one API helper to another.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies old helper calls, separates straightforward replacements from risky cases, and suggests a review order.

output_examples.input: Create a security scan for unsafe HTML injection patterns.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines reusable rules, explains what each rule detects, and lists manual checks for false positives.

best_practices: Preview replacements before using rewrite mode.
Limit searches to relevant directories and languages for clearer results.
Review security pattern matches manually before treating them as vulnerabilities.
anti_patterns: Running broad rewrites without reviewing matches first.
Using plain text search when code structure matters.
Treating every security pattern match as confirmed without context.

faq.question: What tool does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses ast-grep through the sg command-line tool.

faq.question: Does it work without ast-grep installed?
faq.answer: No. Install ast-grep first, then make sure sg is available in your shell.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, and general YAML rule workflows.

faq.question: Can it change files automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, ast-grep supports rewrites, but changes should be previewed and reviewed before committing.

faq.question: Is this a security scanner?
faq.answer: It provides security search patterns, but a human should validate impact and exploitability.

faq.question: When is it better than regex?
faq.answer: Use it when syntax structure matters, such as function calls, imports, hooks, or nested code blocks.
